slides.title: Why industrial digitalization projects mostly fail
slides.subtitle: Every new system gets integrated, customized and deployed from scratch. Cost rises while reuse disappears.

cards.title: No two factories are alike
cards.body: Different equipment, cadence and process make every rollout a new integration and modeling project.

cards.title: Digital systems cost a fortune
cards.body: The license is the small part. Consulting, customization, integration and operations dominate total cost.

cards.title: Fragmented data, tangled integrations
cards.body: Each new application adds another dedicated interface and makes the next change harder.

slides.result: TCO becomes a recurring cost center instead of a compounding operational asset.

slides.title: From Point-to-Point Integration to a Unified Namespace

panels.title: Point-to-point integration
points: Every application connects to every source separately.
Semantic context is duplicated across projects.
A small change breaks multiple interfaces.
Integration cost grows with every new app.
panels.caption: Repeat again and again.

panels.title: Unified Namespace
points: Sources publish once into a governed namespace.
Operational context is shared and reusable.
Applications read and write through one contract.
The next use case starts with the foundation in place.
panels.caption: Build once. Reuse across applications.

slides.title: The foundation is only
slides.note: With governed industrial context in place, the next question is what teams can build on top of it.

slides.title: Start with a valuable use case. Build the reusable foundation behind it.

steps.title: Select a valuable operational use case
steps.body: Choose a use case with clear users, assets, data sources and business outcomes.

steps.title: Build the Unified Data Foundation
steps.body: Create the namespace, establish operational context and connect relevant systems.

steps.body: Generate an application on top of the shared foundation and validate it with users.

steps.body: Add more assets, applications, analytics, digital twins and AI workflows.
